newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher, strong tone dominates.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher, strong tone dominates.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher again Friday after a week with prices sustained by uplifting local news and supportive U.S. Treasuries.

"The market's upward move on Thursday was sustained today. There is a generally good tone," said a trader at a foreign bank. Activity was seasonally slim again, and traders said not many open positions remained open before the anticipated Christmas lull sets in next week.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.39 to 122.59, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 86-3/8.
Another trader said "there was some foreign demand this session. The market is on a relatively strong footing for the year ahead."

Market players listed the decrees signed by President Carlos Menem on labor market reforms signed this week, a number of laws to fight tax evasion passed by Congress and the continuing rebound evidenced by recent economic indicators as the main factors motivating locally generated gains.
In addition, a $6.1 billion stand-by credit facility agreed Friday with a group of international banks to be used by Argentine banks in the event of a liquidity crisis came as welcome news.

However, "until the beginning of the next year, I do not expect much to happen," said the first trader, referring to the expectation that trade will be thin and range-bound in the two last weeks of the year.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.85 percent from 7.05 percent.
